Subject: SCCs: preferred module path & GDPR implications for MedSage DPA

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the call earlier. Our legal team asked us to confirm which SCC module Redwood recommends for our DPA, and whether the same approach covers UK transfers (we're a UK subsidiary of MedSage plc).

High level: we are the data controller; Redwood will process patient de-identified telemetry and analytics data on our behalf. There may be occasional special category fields for clinical consent metadata. We also use US-based analytics providers for batch processing.

Can you: 1) confirm the SCC module you intend to pick, 2) note any additional safeguards we should expect (encryption, subprocessors list), and 3) provide an updated DPA draft or redline that reflects your recommendation?

Appreciate a short summary and any materials we should share with our GC.

Best,

Subject: Re: SCCs: preferred module path & GDPR implications for MedSage DPA

Emily — thanks for the clear summary. Short answers up front:

- Recommended module: Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) — this matches the standard SaaS controller/processor relationship for MedSage as controller and Redwood as processor.
- UK transfers: we apply the UK Addendum alongside the EU SCCs for UK-origin data by default; in practice we keep the same module selection unless the parties' roles differ for UK data.
- Additional safeguards: encryption-in-transit and at-rest for exported exports, strict subprocessors policy, and contractual commitments for onward transfers. For transfers that involve US analytics vendors, we recommend pseudonymization for exported datasets and a documented subprocessors list + access controls.

I'm attaching our short module comparison and a one-page GDPR implications summary for your GC. Vanessa and Rishi — can you review and confirm we can provide a redline DPA that reflects Module 2 + UK Addendum? If MedSage requires joint-controller language for any feature, flag that and we'll route to legal for Module 1 analysis.

Next steps we propose for speed:
- Redwood legal to produce a redline (target 2 business days) reflecting Module 2 + UK Addendum
- MedSage to confirm special categories and any persistent US analytics transfers (Ian?)
- DocuSign send once both sides sign off

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Emily / Marissa — I reviewed the facts as stated. Confirmations and guidance below (legal POV):

1) Module selection: Module 2 is appropriate for the described relationship (MedSage = controller; Redwood = processor). We will prepare a DPA redline with the Module 2 variant of the SCCs.

2) UK coverage: Redwood will attach the UK Addendum alongside the EU SCCs. Where MedSage is transferring UK personal data, the Addendum mirrors the EU SCCs' protections; we will keep the same role mapping unless MedSage explicitly identifies joint-controller responsibilities.

3) Special categories & US analytics: because you noted occasional special category metadata and onward transfers to US analytics vendors, we'll include:
   - contractual requirement that MedSage pseudonymize (or redact) special categories before export where feasible,
   - encryption-at-rest and in-transit obligations,
   - documented subprocessors list + 30-day notification for new subprocessors,
   - a requirement for subprocessors to have equivalent SCCs in place for onward transfers.

4) Practical note on Module boundaries: if any feature requires MedSage and Redwood to make joint decisions about processing purposes (e.g., MedSage opts us to run analytics and retains direct access to raw identifiers), please highlight that — it could push us into a joint-controller discussion (Module 1), which requires different operational and liability allocations.

I've attached a short redline template and a one-page summary you can share with GC. Marissa — please confirm we can send the DocuSign-ready redline once MedSage confirms the special categories and any persistent US processing (> occasional batch).

- Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Quick clarifying Qs before we finalize the redline:

1) Can MedSage confirm whether any of the telemetry datasets contain persistent identifiers (MRN, national ID) that will be accessible to Redwood engineers for debugging? If yes, we need an operational control that limits access and documents retention timelines.

2) Please confirm whether US analytics vendors will receive identifiers or only pseudonymized aggregates. If identifiers flow to the US, we'll add a subprocessor controls section and a short audit-rights clause.

If Emily/Ian can answer those two points we can finalize the Module 2 redline and include the UK Addendum clauses.

- Rishi Malhotra
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Turner <emily.turner@medsage.com>

Thanks all — quick answers:

1) Persistent identifiers: we will not provide national IDs or MRNs to Redwood in production. Access for debugging may include hashed patient IDs (pseudonymized) under strict access controls.

2) US analytics vendors: they will receive pseudonymized aggregates only. No direct identifiers will be sent to US vendors for routine analytics.

We reviewed the attachments and are comfortable with Module 2 + UK Addendum. Please send the redline for signature.

Attaching our proposed DPA draft from procurement for your reference.

Best,
Emily
